code_alterations_with_rationale.why: Initial code assumed WALCHE had a separate loops/ directory. Confirmed the loop registry lives in core/, not loops/. Incorrect path would cause C2 and C7 checks to always fail even on a healthy WALCHE install.
Wrong class name. The actual class in backend/memory/reflection_memory.py is PersistentReflectionMemory, not ReflectionMemory. Mismatch would cause C4 memory check to report false failures.
The module is core/rubric.py, not core/rubric_scorer.py. Also added fallback to try class name Rubric if RubricScorer not found, since WALCHE may use either. Makes C5 check more resilient.
Actual WALCHE module is forensic_cognition, not forensic_logger. Wrong name would cause C6 forensic logging check to always report unavailable.

code_alterations_with_rationale.change: Removed loops/ from architecture health directory check
code_alterations_with_rationale.why: loops/ does not exist as a standalone directory in WALCHE. Loop infrastructure lives in core/. Including it in C11 arch health check would cause false WARN on every healthy WALCHE install.
Module name correction. Actual module is core/provenance.py. C10 check would always fail with wrong name.

code_alterations_with_rationale.change: C7 loop integration — changed from scanning loops/ dir to checking core loop modules directly
code_alterations_with_rationale.why: Loop modules (pain_engine, pain_fmea, healing_engine, spine_guardian, orchestrator, vll) all live in core/. Scanning a non-existent loops/ directory would give misleading results.

code_alterations_with_rationale.change: Import target alignment — added core.guardrail.Guardrail and core.forensic_cognition to C1
code_alterations_with_rationale.why: These are critical WALCHE modules. Guardrail is a hard requirement for safe operation. forensic_cognition provides audit trail. Both needed in C1 import check for accurate baseline.

git_commits.commit: Add WALCHE diagnostic and apply tools
git_commits.what: Five standalone Python tools committed to walche_tools/: loop_audit.py, walche_deep_scan.py, walche_validate.py, walche_apply.py, fix_walche.py
git_commits.why: Needed a complete, runnable diagnostic suite that works against the live WALCHE install without modifying WALCHE core. Tools operate as external diagnostic layer.

git_commits.commit: Add constitutional CLAUDE.md and corpus log
git_commits.what: CLAUDE.md with 11 constitutional laws, corpus/session_log.jsonl initialized
git_commits.why: CLAUDE.md is the persistent memory and constraint layer. Without it every session starts blind. 11 laws encode the operating contract between user and Claude across all platforms and sessions.

git_commits.commit: Add initial corpus intelligence from full session transcript
git_commits.what: corpus/initial_corpus_intelligence.json with 89 URLs, 8 WALCHE modules, 23 construction sources, 11 research papers
git_commits.why: First ingestion baseline. All prior session knowledge captured in structured form so future WALCHE intelligence can be seeded from real work history, not cold start.

loop_audit_checks.C3: Prompt Validation — prompt files exist and PromptManager importable
loop_audit_checks.C5: Rubric Scorer — RubricScorer/Rubric has score()/evaluate() method
loop_audit_checks.C6: Forensic Logging — forensic_cognition importable, logs/ dir writable
loop_audit_checks.C7: Loop Integration — loop_registry + pain_engine, pain_fmea, healing_engine, spine_guardian, orchestrator, vll all importable
loop_audit_checks.C8: Guardrail Interface — Guardrail has check() or evaluate() method
loop_audit_checks.C9: Self-Tests — runs test_*.py files, reports pass rate

deep_scan_checks.S5: EPM contamination — EPM-STARK, WOM-STARK, hardcoded EPM paths inside WALCHE
